title: Cooling system, temperature plausibility and thermal derate
whatItIs: Coolant and intake temperatures change fuel strategy, spark timing, fan load, air density and knock margin. A thermal fault can look like fuel or ignition loss unless temperature is included.
normalValues: A warmed gasoline engine usually stabilizes near its thermostat/fan control range. IAT should be plausible relative to ambient and underhood heat soak.
deviations: Stuck-open thermostat can keep warmup enrichment active too long
Overheating can trigger timing retard and torque reduction
False-high IAT can reduce calculated air density and timing
Fan or alternator load can reveal electrical weakness
influence: Thermal state changes every other diagnosis. Cold-start and hot-idle graphs must not be interpreted with the same thresholds.
checks: Check fan command and actual temperature response
Inspect thermostat, radiator, cap, pump and air pockets
